## Part B: Proposed questionnaire changes

Collected from every card's "Maps to". A row is one change to one question (or one part of the interview); where several cards propose parts of the same change, the card column lists all of them. Entries that only confirm a current option or default are left out; added visual samples are included, because they change what the question shows. "Kept" inside a change means the card confirms that part. Where a card records that part of its change is already in the app (checked by the card writers on 2026-09-28), the row says what is done and what is still open. Evidence lists the sources and standards the card cites for that change; the card's own Evidence line has the full list. Rows are in `questions.json` order, with proposed questions after their family.

Notes for maintainers, found while assembling (details under "Open questions / gaps"):
- **Two option lists for one proposed question.** DC-L19-129 and DC-L19-156 both feed proposed Q-pattern-15 (when to create an account), but with different option ids (`none`, `before-use`, `after-value` against `no-account`, `account-first`, `after-first-use`). DC-L19-129 says it uses DC-L19-156's ids, and that DC-L19-156 still calls the question a follow-up under Q-pattern-07; neither is true of the current DC-L19-156. The table lists DC-L19-129's ids and names the difference.
- **Two floors for one option.** DC-L19-08 proposes 55% (light) and 50% (dark) for body text under Q-color-22 `opacity-levels`; DC-L19-23 proposes 60% and 50% for secondary text.
- **Planned questions.** Changes to Q-pattern-05, Q-dist-01, Q-dist-02, Q-dist-03, Q-pref-01 and Q-pref-02 take effect only when those questions are built; the new lint rules all land on planned Q-dist-03, and the paywall, pricing, streak and permission checks on planned Q-pattern-05.
- **Unnumbered new questions and fields.** The theme-switch question (DC-L19-16), letter alternates (DC-L19-28), toast position and color (DC-L19-113), phone sheet heights (DC-L19-115), sidebar order (DC-L19-118), the AI workspace parts (DC-L19-138), the sign-in order (DC-L19-156) and the Swift version (DC-L19-157) have no id yet.
- **Settled since the last assembly.** The Q-plat id clash is gone (DC-L19-96 is Q-plat-11 again, and DC-L19-151 is Q-plat-15), and DC-L19-130 withdrew Q-pattern-10 in favour of DC-L19-83's Q-motion-12.

## Part C: Conflicts with existing research

Every place a card records that the trusted sources differ from an existing Decision Card (DC-L01 to DC-L18, L09 benchmarks), from the L13 research tables, from a current question default or option, or from what the engine does today. The resolution is the card's proposal; the card id is at the end of each resolution. Where a house standard decides, it is named, and it wins. Where a card records that the app has since changed (checked by the card writers on 2026-09-28), the resolution says what is done and what is still open. The shape and depth rows come from that area's own conflicts table. Disagreements between two sources, with no existing card involved, are listed under "Open questions / gaps".

| Existing card or default | What the sources say | Resolution proposed |
|---|---|---|
| DC-L01-17 (hover one step, press two steps toward more contrast) | One video steps darker on hover in both modes, which in dark mode moves toward less contrast [S-L19-039]; another lightens on hover [S-L19-051] | Keep toward-more-contrast as the default; record both videos as disagreements, not overrides; the direction becomes a zoom-3 sub-choice of Q-color-20 (DC-L19-07) |
| DC-L10-17 (no app-only appearance setting on Apple platforms) | A macOS example app keeps light and dark in its settings popover [S-L19-067] | Keep following the system; DC-L10-17 stays the rule on Apple platforms; the in-app switch is recorded, not adopted (DC-L19-14, DC-L19-142) |
| Q-theme-01 `light-only` (engine sets `darkMode: False`) | STD-visual-details-24 wants both modes generated | `light-first` and `dark-first` still generate both modes; for `dark-only` it is a rename (DC-L19-14) |
| Engine's opaque `color.border.*` for decorative edges (conflict note on STD-visual-details-14) | A 10% see-through ring [S-L19-103]; one video also uses an opaque 85% border [S-L19-039] | See-through ring for decorative edges, the 3:1 border for interactive boundaries; the opaque border stays an option but the standard wins (DC-L19-09) |

## Open questions / gaps

### Found while assembling this file

- **Two option lists for proposed Q-pattern-15.** DC-L19-129 lists `none`, `before-use`, `after-value`, `before-paywall` and `after-personalising` and says they are DC-L19-156's ids; DC-L19-156 lists `account-first`, `after-first-use`, `after-personalising` and `no-account` (and adds `before-paywall`) and says they are DC-L19-129's. DC-L19-129 also says DC-L19-156 "still describes this as the follow-up under Q-pattern-07", but the current DC-L19-156 names Q-pattern-15. One set of ids should be chosen in `_cards/patterns.md` and `_cards/platforms.md`; Part B lists DC-L19-129's and names the difference.
- **Two opacity floors.** Q-color-22 `opacity-levels` gets 55%/50% for body text from DC-L19-08 and 60%/50% for secondary text from DC-L19-23; DC-L19-46 says DC-L19-08 proposes "the floor". Both are [inferred] from contrast arithmetic; one rule should be chosen.
- **Option name mismatch.** DC-L19-188 says DC-L19-171 adds an option `aspect-files` to Q-dist-02; DC-L19-171 says it adds no option and gives the existing `rules` option its shape.
- **Unnumbered new questions and fields** need ids: the theme-switch question (DC-L19-16), letter alternates (DC-L19-28), toast position and color (DC-L19-113), phone sheet heights (DC-L19-115), sidebar order (DC-L19-118), the AI workspace parts (DC-L19-138), the sign-in order (DC-L19-156) and the Swift version (DC-L19-157).
- **Planned targets.** Many proposals land on questions the interview skips today (Q-pattern-05, Q-dist-01 to Q-dist-03, Q-pref-01, Q-pref-02); every new lint rule from the layout and patterns cards waits for Q-dist-03, and the pricing, paywall, streak, permission and store checks wait for Q-pattern-05.
- **Stale notes in two area files.** The motion file's gaps still say that Q-motion-12 and Q-pattern-10 are the same question and one should be kept; DC-L19-130 has since withdrawn Q-pattern-10. The platforms file's gaps say this research file "still shows the old ids until it is rebuilt"; this assembly rebuilds it with Q-plat-11 for DC-L19-96 and Q-plat-15 for DC-L19-151. Both notes are copied below unchanged.
- **Settled since the 2026-09-27 assembly.** The Q-plat id clash (DC-L19-96 is Q-plat-11 again), DC-L19-129's stale pointer to "Q-plat-14" and a `teach-in-onboarding` option (it now points to DC-L19-151's Q-plat-15), and the duplicate rare-moments question (asked once, as Q-motion-12).

### Color (from the area file)

- Hover direction in dark mode is disputed: [S-L19-039] steps darker, [S-L19-051] lighter on hover, DC-L01-17 toward more contrast. No source tested it with users.
- The engine's dark surface steps (about 3.1% brightness apart for a pure gray) are narrower than the videos' 4 to 6%. This was worked out from engine constants, not from a generated palette; a generated build should confirm it before the check is added.
- "Gray 950" in [S-L19-103] may be Tailwind's gray or neutral 950 (the page had just been switched to neutral grays), so the ring's exact contrast is approximate.
- The Tailwind 50/500 and 950/300 pairs in [S-L19-070] were not contrast-checked by the source or here.
- How far the equal-lightness chart palette can stretch before series become hard to tell apart for color-blind people is untested.

### Shape and depth (from the area file)

- The first-tooltip delay has no value from a house source; the only number is one video's 1s [S-L19-079].
- The gradient scrim's stops and opacities are not given by any source; they need measuring from the shared Figma files or setting by contrast tests.
- The Figma values for clay, metal, glass cards and the light-gray shadows are shown on screen only; they should be measured before any becomes a preset.
- Should a sheet that materializes with blur be allowed the 20px of the static toolbar sample? STD-enter-exit-origin-30 says no for animated blur; the standards owner should confirm the split between static and animated blur.
- Feather Icons is recommended twice but is not in DC-L05-01's list; its license and upkeep need checking before it is offered.
- The screenshot-frame values (5% well, 10% ring, 8px inset, 64px hero padding) come from one video in Tailwind's scale; they should be confirmed on a second product before becoming defaults beyond `well`.
- No question records who pays or how old the audience is (Q-aud-01 and Q-aud-02 cover how often and what is at stake). DC-L19-75's new check and DC-L19-79's show-if need that input; should Q-aud-02 or the Q-img-04 hook ask for it?
- Realistic over cartoon [S-L19-111], a realistic AI persona [S-L19-111] and the value of personalized paywall images [S-L19-106] each rest on one guest's self-reported tests. A second source, or the person's own test, should confirm them before any becomes a default.
- Where does a companion mascot's attachment end and pressure begin [S-L19-105]? DC-L19-77 draws the line at guilt and scolding [inferred]; the deceptive-pattern lint (DC-L13-15) has no rule for characters yet.
- The kaleidoscope, clay and metal values are only on screen [S-L19-058], and the glow's 24px blur is from one Figma prototype [S-L19-059]; none should become a preset without measuring and a code translation.

### Motion (from the area file)

- The first tooltip's delay has only one number in the sources (1s, a single video [S-L19-079]); the house fixes only that neighbouring tooltips open instantly.
- No source gives a spinner's rotation period; "fast" is the only guidance [S-L19-003].
- In-app reduced-motion switches (Q-aud-04) and per-device motion budgets (DC-L14-08, TV, watch, car, headset) are not covered by any L19 source.
- Swipe-to-confirm for irreversible actions rests on one video [S-L19-035]; it may deserve a place beside hold-to-confirm, but only after another source agrees.
- Whether a sampled CSS `linear()` spring is ever good enough on the web is open: it is cheaper than a JS library but cannot take a release velocity [inferred].
- STD-enter-exit-origin-39 records a tension between mirrored easing on reversible transitions and the ban on ease-in; these cards follow the ease-out rule.
- Whether the 3% press scale should be dropped under reduced motion is my reading of STD-accessibility-motion-02, not something a source says about press feedback directly.
- Two practitioner videos animate keyboard-initiated actions (the macOS quick-save panel [S-L19-067], the shortcut hint animation [S-L19-079]); the house forbids it (STD-when-to-animate-06), and only their state-change feedback is used here.
- Two Mobbin videos use a vibration to draw attention to a one-time offer [S-L19-104] [S-L19-107]. The cards read this as outside STD-springs-gestures-61, since an offer appearing is not success, error, commit or snap; the videos do not say whether the vibration answers the person's own tap, so the reading is [inferred].
- Onboarding sits in two house tiers: STD-when-to-animate-08 gives onboarding steps standard motion, while STD-when-to-animate-09 lists onboarding and first run among delight moments. Mobbin's examples (animated loading and verification in Bump, a character across 61 screens in Bipul) [S-L19-107] animate the whole flow. These cards split it: steps and waits get standard or state motion, the first open, a character and the first success get the delight [inferred].
- The streak video's point that surprise motion keeps a routine engaging comes with its own warning that engagement is not habit [S-L19-105]; no source measures whether milestone-only celebration keeps people coming back as well as frequent surprises do.
- Proposed Q-motion-12 and DC-L19-130's Q-pattern-10 are the same question; the maintainers should keep one.
- Mobbin says its library holds animations from shipped products (S-L19-108), a possible place to find the real-product visual samples these cards name (Runkeeper's opening, Opal's milestones and stories); that is Mobbin's own claim, and its MCP needs sign-in.

### Platforms (from the area file)

- The 50-pixel drag strip (DC-L19-150) and the 70-80% right-handed figure (DC-L19-145) come from one video each; no platform source in this wiki confirms either.
- Windows desktop apps have no practitioner or house source in this wiki; DC-L19-149 and DC-L19-150 lean on macOS only.
- Swipe-to-confirm (DC-L19-146): the sources give no tap alternative; hold-to-confirm is the house pattern, but no source compares the two for high-impact, non-destructive actions such as sending.
- Whether `brand-first` (Q-plat-05) should stay as an option for Flutter, where the React Native standards do not apply, is open; the sources are silent on Flutter.
- The proposed thresholds (a ⌘K palette above about five sections in DC-L19-152) are inferred, not sourced.
- None of the sources cover screen-reader testing, forced colors, text direction or video captions beyond one changelog line [S-L19-001]; DC-L10-16 and Q-gov-07 remain the reference.
- The store and payment facts in DC-L19-155 are dated and narrow: Apple's early-2026 rejections [S-L19-104], and one founder's self-reported US iOS and Android experience in 2026 [S-L19-111]. No house or platform source in this wiki confirms them; they need re-checking before they become builder errors.
- Markets have no home in the interview. The onboarding video says, with no source, that users in Eastern markets are more comfortable with information-heavy screens [S-L19-107]; Moonly says hard paywalls won in the US while soft ones won elsewhere, and its host and guest disagree on this [S-L19-111]; the savings app ranks people locally to allow for currency and income differences [S-L19-078]. Stage 02 asks who uses the product but not where; whether a market question belongs next to Q-aud-01 is open [inferred].
- Web push permission, sharing from the web and sign-in on the web have no source (DC-L19-154, DC-L19-156, DC-L19-158 lean on phone apps).
- No source says how a SwiftUI system should hand tokens and styles to components (environment values, button styles, view modifiers), and Jetpack Compose has no house code standard (DC-L19-157, DC-L19-148).
- Proposed question ids: Q-plat-11 is DC-L19-96's slowest-device question and Q-plat-15 is DC-L19-151's keyboard-shortcut question; `_cards/motion.md` moved DC-L19-96 back to Q-plat-11 on 2026-09-28, and `_cards/patterns.md` now names DC-L19-151's question Q-plat-15 with its `learn-by-doing` split, so the clash is settled in the cards (the generated `research/L19-learning-wiki.md` still shows the old ids until it is rebuilt). The new proposals here are Q-plat-16 to Q-plat-18; account timing is DC-L19-129's proposed Q-pattern-15, which DC-L19-156 extends.
- The free-trial toggle rule (DC-L19-155) rests on one video [S-L19-104]; three cards now repeat it (DC-L19-106, DC-L19-139, DC-L19-155), all as dated behaviour to re-check. No card should turn it into a builder error until a platform source confirms it.

### Tokens (from the area file)

- The Tailwind easing values and the bare `transition` class's default timing function in DC-L19-184 come from Tailwind's own documentation, not from an L19 source; they were checked on 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-27 and can change with a Tailwind release.
- No source says how native apps should scale spacing with Dynamic Type; DC-L19-182 only settles the web.
- Whether radii should follow rem is untested; DC-L19-182 keeps them px because the standard's check covers only margin, padding and gap.
- Should the engine's reduced-motion and theme attributes (`[data-motion]`, `[data-theme]`) also be documented as the "state attributes" of the page, next to the component ones? Not covered by the sources.
- How `engine.py review` should rate a hand-typed curve (must-level break of STD-visual-details-26, or LOW polish per [S-L19-027]) is still open, as the tokens synthesis notes.

### Typography, layout, components and patterns (gaps stated inside the cards)

- The 16px mobile-web body size still rests on DC-L02-20 and one video; only the 16px input size is a house standard (DC-L19-32).
- The sources give no native equivalent for balanced and pretty line wrapping (DC-L19-30).

- No source gives a spinner duration beyond "fast" (DC-L19-127).
- Pricing: taxes, currencies, local prices and monthly-or-yearly switches on web pages are still not covered, and no source settles where anchoring turns into misleading framing, so that stays a human review (DC-L19-134); no source weighs the fairness of prices that vary by device or network (DC-L19-135).
- Mobile paywalls and free trials now have sources, but they are one consultant's experience across two videos [S-L19-104] [S-L19-106] (DC-L19-139); app-store analytics tools are not covered (DC-L19-137), and neither are native mobile AI patterns (DC-L19-138).
- The claim that a coined metric name stops people switching comes with no data [S-L19-110] (DC-L19-38, DC-L19-136).

### Process sources not carried into cards (from the area file)

- **Pricing and client work** ([S-L19-036], most of [S-L19-038], the prices in [S-L19-072]): hourly, project and value-based pricing, niches and add-on services are about the designer's business, not the system, so they change no question. The transferable ideas (the need behind the request, before-and-after results) are in DC-L19-166 and DC-L19-177. Two sources note that work takes longer than planned ([S-L19-036]; four screens took three days instead of four to six hours in [S-L19-078]); `pacing.json` already labels its minutes as rough estimates.
- **Where to host a portfolio and how many projects to show** ([S-L19-037], [S-L19-064]): career advice with no interview change.
- **Resource lists** ([S-L19-073], [S-L19-049], [S-L19-082]): named sites for placeholder logos, stock photos, mockups and icons could feed DC-L17-04's fallback order, but their licences were not checked here and one presenter jokes about taking logos, so none is proposed as a default.
- **Figma effect recipes and animated prototypes** ([S-L19-058], [S-L19-071], [S-L19-081]) belong to the surface-effects and motion cards (DC-L19-67, DC-L19-85 to DC-L19-99).
- **Moonly's paywall, pricing, onboarding and imagery results** ([S-L19-111]): one paywall for all features, soft versus hard paywalls, price anchors and units, free trials, a 30-screen onboarding tailored to the ad, realistic imagery and the AI guide's look belong to the patterns and imagery cards (DC-L19-129, DC-L19-135, DC-L19-137, DC-L19-75). Its payment advice (an alternative to Apple's payments in the US, avoiding Android's alternative billing) depends on store rules as of 2026 and is a business choice, not a system one. Only its process and launch lessons are used here (DC-L19-161 to -166, -177, -179).
- **The dashboard patterns** ([S-L19-110]): insights beside charts, recaps, fitted visuals, coined metrics and AI explaining a change belong to the dashboard and retention cards (DC-L19-122, DC-L19-136). Its figure that AI dashboards get about twice the saves and exports on Mobbin shows what designers collect, not what users prefer. Only the screenshot gut check and "one screenshot that tells what the product does" are used here (DC-L19-167, -170, -177, -179).
- **Mobbin's promo video** ([S-L19-109]) has no narration; it contributes only the library's self-reported size and scope (DC-L19-161, DC-L19-178).

Also noted in the process cards: no source covers the licence terms of the screen library the research step studies (DC-L19-161), Android store pages, or the share-image sizes each platform specifies (DC-L19-179).

### Disagreements between sources

These involve no existing card; each card records how it settles them.
- Hover direction: one video steps darker on hover, another lightens (DC-L19-07).
- Dark card borders: "brighten" advice against a light border lowered because it had too much contrast (DC-L19-05).
- Text color: two videos use near-black text and, in dark mode, light gray with white reserved; one uses plain black or white; one flips dark-mode text to white (DC-L19-08).
- Hiding actions: one Kole Jain video collapses busy card buttons into a menu, another says to line them up on a new edge first; settled by how often the action is used [inferred] (DC-L19-44, DC-L19-105, DC-L19-123).
- Delete confirmations: two Kole Jain videos disagree on which button carries the fill (DC-L19-107).
- The phone tab bar's main action: broken out of the bar in one video, dropped into line in another; they agree when the action is the most used one [inferred] (DC-L19-119, DC-L19-145).
- Commitment labels on buttons: a big win at Duolingo [S-L19-105], hit or miss for the paywall consultant [S-L19-104] (DC-L19-38).
- Prompting people to share: Emil Kowalski relies on quality reaching a few of the right people [S-L19-007], Moonly builds a one-tap share flow [S-L19-111]; they sell different things, so neither result transfers without a test [inferred] (DC-L19-179).
- Practitioner motion the house standards override: animated keyboard-started actions and shortcut hints (DC-L19-151, STD-when-to-animate-06), a quick panel that slides in (DC-L19-149), a spring-driven Figma spinner (DC-L19-127), an ease-in-out fade-in (DC-L19-85, DC-L19-133), a bouncy tooltip (DC-L19-70), signature screen transitions on native (DC-L19-146), and a vibration that fires as an offer appears (DC-L19-83, DC-L19-98, DC-L19-146; STD-springs-gestures-61).

A second, adversarial pass on the same day re-read every cited source and the current standards: DC-L19-116's default contradicted STD-visual-details-20 and was fixed; DC-L19-101, -102, -107, -109, -110, -112, -113, -114 and -117 were corrected for stale question or standard status, token names the standards now fix, a one-video claim, or a missing keyboard rule. No card was withdrawn.

### Patterns (from the area file)

A second pass on the same day checked every card against its cited sources, the house standards, questions.json and the sibling cards. It corrected two attributions (fake urgency is the paywall video narrator's point, not the consultant's; the paywall that says paying unlocks everything is Orbit's, shown in the Moonly video), an outdated quote of DC-L19-83, a wrong claim that Q-color-19 has no light-to-dark ramp, and easing in two preloader recipes. It also aligned DC-L19-129's account options with DC-L19-156, DC-L19-130's metadata key with DC-L19-83, and DC-L19-128 with STD-components-toasts-drawers-15. No card was withdrawn.
